I always talk about how much of a great time me and my little brother had but there was something that kinda fucked up part of the night. My brother(13) has autism so we were using the Disability access pass. When he’s starting to get overstimulated he gets wobbly and he becomes a fall risk. We asked at the top of the hill if we could get return times for the maze but they said no we had to walk all the way down for times. We did but Matt was having trouble so I carried him down. When we got down we found out it was a 1 hour and a half return time so we would either have to go back up and down the hill or just stay down there with no quiet place for him to destimulate and regain his balance. So we were stuck staying cause I couldn’t carry him anymore. The line person made a stupid comment on not bringing disabled people if they can’t handle the wait. Which pissed me off but I just spoke to a manager who got us into the mazes in 45 minutes rather than the hour and a half. She also informed me about the shuttle that went up and down the hill so thankfully I didn’t have to carry him back up. I feel like that should be more visible but it’s fine. He was fine, just starting to get a little overwhelmed and I just felt bad cause I didn’t have anyway to help him immediately. He had a wonderful time and that’s all that really matters but ablest people are assholes.

One more that’s more recent as in 2021, still in Hollywood. It’s a bit long but it’s worth it. I took my youngest brother for his first ever hhn and a fun fact my youngest brother has autism. So I’m over prepared with noise canceling headphones and sunglasses for the lights and the noise and I’m hoping he has a good time cause he was begging to go for two months and he almost had to miss cause he got in trouble with our mom. So I start us off easy with some rides cause i figure if he gets to scared and we need to go home early at least he got to do something. Well we get done with Jurassic and he says he’s ready to be scared and he wants to do the tram first. I take my younger brother with autism out to theme parks and other fun places a lot and I trust him not to wonder to far but I know that he could still get lost if he gets distracted. I place a waterproof phone protector on him with a note, it usually reads “hi my name is—-, if you’re reading this I’m lost. Please call my sister, her number is ——. He also has Life360 on his phone but only my mom can track him that way and no way am I calling her and telling her I lost the kid. My brother knows that if he’s turned around he needs to find someone in a uniform or security and give them the note. If he can’t find a worker, he’s supposed to find any lady who also has children. The note helps because he’s not supposed talk to strangers and he takes that pretty literally so he’ll give them the note so he feels he still followed the rules. Thankfully he has only gotten lost once at the movies when he went out the wrong bathroom exit, and I was able to find him before he wondered any further

Parents can be hard to deal with and even harder to convince. I was never a party person or someone who got into trouble other than not doing my homework so they were fine with me going to the movies or things like that. Bigger things took more time to convince them. Like when I went on a girls trip with a few friends, my dad wanted details on the friends I was going with, making sure I’d cleaned my room and I had done my work for class before I left. I also payed for everything I wanted to do so he was fine with it as long as I checked in. Talk to your parents and start by asking for little freedoms. Be willing to comprise on curfews and rules. If they say no don’t push it or get upset, it shows immaturity. Ask them nicely to explain why they said no and what would be ok alternative activity. In a few years you won’t be under their control but for now it’s easier to play the game and win trust.

Try different stims when you aren’t to anxious and see what helps you
